doors.title: Win Trust Two
doors.audience: For teams that need customer assurance, readiness evidence, or a faster path through diligence.
triggers: An enterprise deal or renewal is blocked by assurance requirements.
A customer, insurer, or investor is asking for evidence you cannot assemble quickly.
AI adoption is creating new customer questions about ownership and control.
doors.tension: The business is ready to grow, but proof is scattered across policies, systems, and people.
doors.gap: The gap is between having good intentions and being able to show repeatable evidence when the buyer asks.
doors.decision: Choose the evidence and operating work that turns readiness into buyer confidence.

opening.text: Your buyer isn't asking whether you're secure. They're asking whether you can prove it by Friday.
opening.source: The Forcing Function §06, approved opening line

stat.text: 61% were required to hold a certification to win or renew a contract.

statSecondary.text: 68% of companies have one or fewer full-time security people, while 93% call security a top priority.

serviceFamilies.name: ISMS, SSPP, and statement of applicability

proof.text: No formal security program, then SOC 2 Type I with zero findings and multi-entity SOC 2 Type II across a software portfolio.
proof.basis: Transit Technologies engagement, published customer story

program.snapshot: A Snapshot scoped to the actual obligation, so you know what the contract requires and what it does not.
program.build: A readiness program with continuous evidence on AiVRIC.
program.operate: A managed program with questionnaire ownership and auditor management, so the engineering team goes back to shipping.
program.source: The Forcing Function §02, What 3HUE sells them

doors.title: Gain Control
doors.audience: For ownership and operating teams that need shared visibility, leverage, and governance across multiple companies.
triggers: A new platform acquisition or portfolio review needs a common view.
Board, lender, or investor reporting is inconsistent across holdings.
The portfolio needs more control without adding a full internal team.
doors.tension: Important risk and technology decisions are being made company by company without a shared operating picture.
doors.gap: The gap is between local activity and portfolio-level oversight that can guide investment, sequencing, and accountability.
doors.decision: Create a repeatable governance rhythm that gives leaders visibility without slowing operators down.

opening.text: Your bigger competitors run cyber diligence on 81% of deals. You run it on 29%.
opening.source: The Forcing Function §06, approved opening line

stat.text: Sponsors above $25B AUM include cybersecurity in transaction diligence 81% of the time. Below $25B, only 29% do.

statSecondary.text: 26% of firms have seen a reduced valuation or exit price after a cyber finding.

proof.text: 1,000+ systems certified under one scalable assessment framework.
proof.basis: A large North American bank, published customer story, client unnamed

program.build: One control set applied across every operating company, isolated per entity.
program.operate: Quarterly board- and investment-committee-ready reporting, with the fund seeing one view.
program.source: The Forcing Function §02, What 3HUE sells them

share.title: Gain Control: See and govern what matters. · 3HUE
share.description: For ownership and operating teams that need shared visibility, leverage, and governance across multiple companies.

doors.title: Stay Ready
doors.audience: For regulated and risk-heavy operators that need clear ownership, resilience, response, and evidence that survives scrutiny.
triggers: An examiner request, audit finding, or remediation deadline is active.
An incident or continuity concern exposes a readiness gap.
Regulatory, privacy, or AI adoption pressure is crossing operational boundaries.
doors.tension: The organization cannot afford to discover ownership or evidence gaps during an examination or incident.
doors.gap: The gap is between documented plans and an operating model that stays ready when conditions change.
doors.decision: Establish the accountable programs and managed practices that make readiness continuous.

opening.text: Your controls passed in December. The question is what they were doing in March.
opening.source: The Forcing Function §06, approved opening line

stat.text: 72% still rely on periodic assessments; only 28% monitor continuously.
stat.source: RegScale, 2026 State of Continuous Controls Monitoring

statSecondary.text: 86.8% of small businesses have deployed MFA, but only 51.1% require it across all key accounts.

proof.text: Engagements are scoped and delivered by the same practitioner, whose background includes closing FDA 483 observations and remediating bank Matters Requiring Attention under sustained examination.

program.snapshot: Named framework crosswalks in the examiner's language: NIST CSF and 800-53/171 as the spine, mapped to ISO 27001, COBIT, FFIEC, and SOC 2.
program.build: Continuous controls monitoring that replaces point-in-time testing.
program.operate: Remediation that closes findings and keeps them closed, with board-ready risk translation.
program.source: The Forcing Function §02, What 3HUE sells them
